correctness.rationale: The corrected claim was checked on its stated stationary, fixed-parameter domain. The last-reset integral and |V| <= min(b,Sigma A) bound lead to the two squared errors 4r² lambda E[A³]=24 lambda/r and L²r² E[A⁴]/4=6L²/r². Concatenating clipped independent backward windows and exponential tails gives the independent age marks outside a probability m exp(-rd); fourth moments justify the product limits. The standardized covariance is exp(-2 lambda t)/2 for t>0 and 1 at t=0. Age regression and sign independence give the centered integrand covariance exp(-(r+2 lambda)|t-s|); summing squared grid values and interval increment bounds gives 4nT/(r+2 lambda)+2T²/n. Integrating the stationary coupling error then proves the uniform L² limit and the finite-time variance. The linear benchmark follows separately from the generator and covariance ODE; it is not a nonlinear diffusion limit. value.rationale: In a specific persistent active-particle model, the result identifies quantitatively different instantaneous and time-integrated limits. It explains why a non-Gaussian stationary velocity law with a discontinuity in its limiting autocorrelation can coexist with a continuous telegraph-driven displacement.
